Scope: road works, box culverts, open drain channels and dike walls, street lighting and low-voltage cables, and concrete ducts at road crossings. Contract value 52,025,516 SAR excluding VAT, 18 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At 82.1% against 52.3% planned, the project is 29.8% ahead of plan. This week it gained 0.79% against 1.20% planned, below the weekly plan.

Well ahead of plan, but the forecast finish slipped to 28 days after the contract date. The weekly report and the P6 update (UP 35, data date 03-Nov-2026) both forecast completion on 11-Sep-2027, 28 days after the contract completion date of 14-Aug-2027 and six days later than last week. Total float fell from −19 to −24 days. The negative float now runs through the pavement-marking procurement, the asphalt and finishing works on the connection to the 5th Ring Road, testing and commissioning, and close-out. Additional scope on Collector 9 and Road 52 is still open.

Data notes

  • The two summary sheets (files 15 and 16) label a cost-based progress figure as "actual" and give a cost-based planned figure. This report uses physical % complete (man-hour weighted) only.
  • Files 15 and 16 give this week's progress change with opposite signs (negative in file 15, positive in file 16).
  • File 15 names the MODON PM as عبد الله الجليفي and file 16 as عبد الله الشنيفي. File 16 also gives project start 24-Nov-2025 and contract end 23-May-2026, against site handover 15-Feb-2026 and completion 14-Aug-2027 everywhere else.
  • This week's quantities in the summary sheets (files 15 and 16) match the change in the Major Quantities sheet for cut (8,999 m³), subgrade (820 m³) and aggregate base course (1,008 m³), but give fill as 950 m³ against +443.7 m³. The report uses the Major Quantities change. The weekly table has no gain for 13-Oct-2026 because earlier reports were not used.
  • The Tracking Sheet presentation (file 11) repeats last week's cost-based progress figures and gives no physical progress.
  • The revised plan in the Physical-Chart Data sheet is identical to the baseline.
  • The Major Quantities sheet has an older block of items at zero (subgrade 21,604 m³, base course 14,403 m³, kerbs 23,250 "m³", 15 kV cable 5,632 "m²", substation, RMU, 7 m lighting poles and others) next to the current items with progress. Only the current items are used.
  • LV cable: the Major Quantities sheet gives 6,371 of 8,007 m installed; the Progress Summary gives 6,923 of 8,463.65 m.
  • Luminaires are 264 in the Procurement sheet and 247 in the Progress Summary; earthing units 17 and 15. Procurement is 92.8% complete by man-hours although 17 of 18 materials are reported on site.
  • The invoice summary shows 0 submitted invoices although 8 are logged, and a submitted value (44,051,595) 2,000 SAR below the consultant-approved value (44,053,595). The revised contract value and EAC cells also hold 21,100,000 and 20,900,000 next to 52,025,516.
  • General Information dates baseline schedule approval 01-Mar-2025, before contract award; the milestone sheet and P6 give 01-Mar-2026. The FIR summary for 28-Oct to 03-Nov lists FIR-0960 dated 27-Oct-2026, before the period.
  • Manual head count in November is 107 against 137 planned in the Manpower sheet, but the trade breakdown in the Weekly Progress Report sheet uses a plan of 105 (107 actual).
  • The risk dashboard (file 17) shows 240 open risks and 133 open issues but zero in every category; the log lists 8 risks, 3 of them open. Culvert 4 and Al Gloud Road are open in the weekly report's risk register but closed in file 17.
  • The P6 milestone table inside the Milestones sheet (for example mobilisation 02-Apr-2026) is out of date; milestone forecasts and float are taken from the P6 file UP 35.
  • The weekly report measures the delay as 28 calendar days; P6 gives −24 days of float. In P6 the open-drain-channel milestone has 14 days of float but the Open Drain Channels WBS −2. The Testing sheet shows testing of the electrical networks at 75% since 20-Oct-2026, against a planned start of 08-May-2027, and testing and commissioning has 3,105 man-hours earned with none planned.
